fields.v: Distinguished the two tools on correctness and user effort with significant differences; single session per participant, not repeated. Order effect: similar correctness effect whichever tool came first, but user effort differed by order, possibly because the agent-first phase showed users how to approach the problem in the later copilot phase (carry-over, Appendix D). Limitations stated: one instance of each tool type; LLM not controlled in the copilot condition; mostly student participants, novice agent users; limited number of tasks; time measurement may not be representative (no multitasking, short sessions); tasks pre-defined, no planning; findings tied to April-May 2025
fields.quote: This may be because even if the agent did not fully solve the problem in the agent-first condition, it showed users how to approach the problem in the subsequent copilot condition.
fields.where: Appendix D.2 User Effort Breakdown, p. 30
fields.why: The authors report an order (carry-over) effect on user effort in the within-participant design, a weakness of the comparison method that the field does not mention.
fields.doubt: No Apêndice D.2 (pág. 29-30) os autores dizem que o esforço difere conforme a ordem (agente primeiro ou Copilot primeiro), talvez porque o agente ensinou o caminho antes da fase Copilot. É uma fraqueza do desenho within-participant. Decide se acrescentas ao campo.
